name: Yaacomo
tagline: German GPU-accelerated relational in-memory DBMS for real-time analytics (c. 2011-2023); defunct.
description: Yaacomo was a relational in-memory database from Q2WEB GmbH in Germany that used massively parallel algorithms on graphics processors (with a CPU fallback) for real-time analytics and big-data queries. Its marketing stressed energy efficiency, claiming server-class performance from a palm-sized, 10-watt device, and it won a GreenIT award in 2011; it was also pitched for embedded and machine-to-machine systems and could run on APUs and mobile hardware. The site stayed online, largely unchanged, into 2023 and has returned 404 since; dbdb.io lists the project as failed. HeavyDB, Kinetica and Brytlyt are active GPU databases.
statusNote: Website static for years and offline by 2025; dbdb.io marks the project as failed (end year 2023). Consider HeavyDB, Kinetica or Brytlyt.
strengths: GPU-parallel query execution for fast analytics on modest hardware
Low power footprint, suited to embedded deployments
weaknesses: Defunct vendor; no downloads or support
Little technical documentation was ever published
useCases: Context for evaluating GPU database vendors
